title: Reputation System
content: Reputation levels run Hated, Hostile, Unfriendly, Neutral, Friendly, Honored, Revered, Exalted. From Neutral it takes 3,000 points to Friendly, 6,000 to Honored, 12,000 to Revered and 21,000 to Exalted, 42,000 in all. Each faction's quartermaster sells more as you climb, and humans gain 10% extra reputation.

title: Auction House
content: Every faction capital has an Auction House, such as Stormwind's Trade District and Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength, and so do Booty Bay, Gadgetzan and Everlook; Dalaran and Shattrath have none. On this realm every auction house is the same market, open to both factions, so it doesn't matter which one you use. Auctions last 12, 24 or 48 hours, the deposit is lost if the item doesn't sell, and the house keeps 15% of a sale.

expert_content: Post on 24 hours and undercut the lowest price by a copper, not by half; if the market is flooded, wait for it to clear instead of racing to the bottom. The house keeps 15% of every sale, so price that in, never list below what a vendor would pay, and park a bank alt next to the auctioneer to save the trip.

title: Quest System
content: Quest givers show a yellow ! when they have a quest and a yellow ? when you can turn one in. A quest's level shows as a color: grey is too low to give much experience, green is easy, yellow is your level, orange is hard and red is well above you. The log holds 25 quests, and most can be shared with your party.

title: Talent System
content: Characters get one talent point per level from level 10, 71 by level 80, spent across their class's three trees. A class trainer resets talents for gold: 1 gold the first time, rising with each respec to a 50 gold cap and dropping back over time. Dual specialization at 40 lets you keep two builds.

title: Glyph System
content: Each character has three major and three minor glyph slots: one of each opens at level 15, another major at 30 and 80, and another minor at 50 and 70. Glyphs are made by scribes with Inscription and sold on the auction house, and putting a new glyph in a slot destroys the old one.

title: Achievement System
content: Press Y to open achievements; they belong to each character and award points, and some give titles, pets or mounts. For example World Explorer gives the title the Explorer, and Higher Learning, reading the books hidden in Dalaran, gives the Kirin Tor Familiar pet. Feats of Strength give no points.

title: Player vs Player Combat
content: Players fight each other in battlegrounds, arenas, Wintergrasp and the open world. Killing enemy players who give honor and winning objectives earns Honor points, spent with PvP vendors on gear. On a PvP realm contested zones flag you automatically; on a PvE realm you flag yourself with /pvp.

title: Mount System
content: Riding is trained in steps: Apprentice (60% ground mounts) at level 20 for 4 gold, Journeyman (100% epic ground) at 40 for 50 gold, Expert (flying) at 60 for 250 gold, Artisan (epic flying) at 70 for 5,000 gold, and Cold Weather Flying, needed to fly in Northrend, at 77 for 1,000 gold. Mounts are bought separately from mount vendors.

title: Pet System
content: Hunters learn Tame Beast and Feed Pet at level 10 and keep beasts as permanent combat pets; Beast Mastery hunters can also tame exotic beasts. Feed Pet takes a food the beast eats, such as meat, fish or bread, and keeps it happy, and an unhappy pet deals less damage. Warlocks summon demons, Death Knights raise a ghoul and frost mages get a Water Elemental. Non-combat companion pets are purely cosmetic followers. Stable masters hold the beasts a hunter isn't using.

title: Guild System
content: The Guild tab of the Social window (O) lists the members and who is online. A member whose rank allows it invites a player with /ginvite and their name, or the tab's Add Member button; /gquit leaves. To found a guild, buy a guild charter from a guild master in a capital, collect signatures and turn it in. The guild leader sets ranks and what each may do, including guild bank withdrawals. Guilds in Wrath have no levels or perks.

title: Death and Your Corpse
content: When you die, release your spirit and you appear as a ghost at the nearest graveyard; run back to your corpse and resurrect there for free. The spirit healer at the graveyard revives you on the spot instead, but from level 11 that costs extra durability on your gear and gives resurrection sickness, weaker stats for up to ten minutes. Every death wears your gear, which a repair vendor fixes for gold.

title: Instance System
content: Dungeons are five-player and Wrath raids are 10 or 25. Heroic dungeon lockouts reset daily and raid lockouts weekly; a normal dungeon can be reset from your portrait menu, but you can enter at most five instances per hour.

title: World Events
content: Yearly holidays, all on the in-game calendar: Lunar Festival (Feb 1-14), Love is in the Air (Feb 10-23), Children's Week (Apr 30-May 6), Midsummer Fire Festival (Jun 21-Jul 4), Brewfest (Sep 20-Oct 4), Hallow's End (Oct 18-31), Pilgrim's Bounty (Nov 21-27) and the Feast of Winter Veil (Dec 15-Jan 2).

title: Profession Specializations
content: Several crafts have a specialization with its own recipes: Blacksmithing has Armorsmith and Weaponsmith (then Axe, Mace or Sword), Leatherworking has Dragonscale, Elemental and Tribal, Tailoring has Mooncloth, Shadoweave and Spellfire, Engineering has Goblin and Gnomish, and Alchemy has Elixir, Potion and Transmutation Master.

title: Currency Systems
content: Besides gold, the currency tab tracks Honor and Arena Points for PvP gear, Emblems of Triumph and Frost for PvE gear, Stone Keeper's Shards from Wintergrasp for its vendors and heirlooms, and Champion's Seals from the Argent Tournament dailies. Honor caps at 75,000.
